clue.text: Wants political biopic shown in bar, Oscar contender

indicators.note: shown in places the wanting-plus-film pieces inside the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban
wants means lacks
W. is Oliver Stone's 2008 biopic of George W. Bush

explanation.surface: An Oscar-tipped film is barred while a political biopic plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2010 ballet thriller starring Natalie Portman was a Best Picture nominee, hence an Oscar contender.

clue.text: Musicians who also made films, unusually able set

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the following words set out in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A band who also made movies, an unusually capable outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liverpool band also starred in films such as A Hard Day's Night and Help!

clue.text: In hall, starting like team of Oscar presenters

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the run of words hall, starting

explanation.surface: Starting in the hall, as befits a glittering group of award presenters.
explanation.definitionFit: A team made entirely of famous performers is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Filmed historic event in Washington (1963) or London (1939)

definitions.text: Filmed historic event in Washington (1963) or London (1939)

parts.words: Filmed historic event in Washington (1963) or London (1939)
parts.note: Martin Luther King's 1963 address at the Lincoln Memorial, and George VI's 1939 wartime broadcast filmed in 2010

explanation.surface: A historic address recorded on film, either in America's capital or in Britain's.
explanation.walkthrough: Both events are royal or King speeches: Martin Luther King's 'I have a dream' in Washington, and King George VI's declaration of war broadcast from London, the subject of the Oscar-winning film.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase fits both the civil-rights leader's oration and the stammering monarch's broadcast dramatised in the 2010 film.

clue.text: Debra and others, players on the fringes

definitions.meaning: Debra Winger the actress plus others of that surname
footballers or hockey players who play out on the wings

explanation.definitionFit: Wide players in team sports, and the plural of an American actress's surname.

clue.text: She's crazy a lot in name part

indicators.note: crazy indicates the letters of the following phrase are jumbled wildly

explanation.surface: A woman who is mad about plenty in the role of the name part.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link word ('is'). Fourteen letters of 'a lot in name part' rearrange to the actress's full name across the two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress who won Best Actress for Black Swan is a woman, so 'she' stands for her.

clue.text: Part of the house acclaimed old movie star

definitions.meaning: the triangular top section of a wall under a pitched roof
Clark, star of Gone with the Wind

explanation.definitionFit: A roof's triangular end wall, and the surname of the Hollywood legend of Gone with the Wind.

clue.text: Fish in area covered by maker of 3 down

indicators.note: covered by means the letter for area goes inside the royal initials

parts.note: the maker of the 1939 King's speech is George VI, initials GR for Georgius Rex

explanation.surface: A fish found in a region overseen by the speechmaking king.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-snouted freshwater fish, also called a garfish or needlefish.

clue.text: Movie agent that's hugging large comic strip heroine

indicators.note: hugging means the agent and the 'that is' letters wrap around the size abbreviation

parts.note: James Bond is cinema's best-known secret agent
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A film spy who is embracing something big, as in a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic Young's long-running American newspaper strip has this woman as its title character.

clue.text: Unfinished Elm Street production in British studio location

indicators.note: Unfinished means each of the two words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An incomplete Nightmare on Elm Street shoot at an English film studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts the end off both 'Elm' and 'Street'; 'production' is a link, suggesting a film shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hertfordshire town is home to famous film and television studios near London.

clue.text: Director and actor taking part in challenge

indicators.note: taking part in signals that the letters form part of the following word

explanation.surface: A filmmaker who also performs enters a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody, the New York filmmaker, both directs and acts in his own pictures.

clue.text: Common sense about where Bing and Bob went in 1947 in Hitchcock classic

indicators.note: about says the sense word goes around the destination phrase

parts.note: nous is common sense

parts.words: where Bing and Bob went in 1947
parts.note: Bing Crosby and Bob Hope made the 1947 film Road to Rio, so they went to Rio

explanation.surface: Ordinary good sense concerning the Crosby and Hope road movie and a Hitchcock thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Road to' films took Crosby and Hope to various places; 1947's was Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1946 spy thriller with Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman is a celebrated Hitchcock film.

clue.text: Allowed line introducing Spielberg hit

parts.note: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial was a Spielberg blockbuster

explanation.surface: A line permitted to introduce a Spielberg blockbuster.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to have allowed it; past tense of the verb meaning permit.

clue.text: Absorbing story blends peril with disruption

indicators.note: with disruption tells us the letters of blends peril are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A gripping tale mixes danger with chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that holds you rapt, like a gripping tale, is described as one that enthrals.

clue.text: Crenelation reconstructed for historical epic

indicators.note: reconstructed means the letters of the battlement word are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Castle battlements rebuilt for a sweeping period film.
explanation.definitionFit: D.W. Griffith's 1916 silent film spanning several eras is a landmark historical epic.

clue.text: Comic strips used without copyright for film texts

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled strips go around the letter
Comic suggests something funny and mixed up, so strips is rearranged

explanation.surface: Cartoon strips reused with no copyright for movie screenplays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means 'outside'; 'used' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Screenplays are the written texts actors work from in making a film.

clue.text: Far from average former great actor holding leading part in movie

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: holding means the actor's name wraps around the first letter

parts.note: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a great Victorian actor-manager

indicators.note: leading part in picks out the first letter of movie

explanation.surface: An ex-star of the stage takes a lead role in a film that is anything but ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extreme lies at the far end of a scale, nowhere near the middle.

clue.text: Location of many catches, where "Jaws" was partly filmed

definitions.meaning: the sea, where fishermen make their catches
the shark film was shot partly out at sea

explanation.definitionFit: A literary term for the ocean, also the title of a 1977 Peter Benchley adaptation.

clue.text: Use part in unconventional way — it's what many an Oscar winner does

definitions.text: it's what many an Oscar winner does

indicators.note: in unconventional way says the letters of use part are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: Playing a role unconventionally is what wins Oscars.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrasal verb in the third person: an emotional winner cries at the podium.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcome winners often weep on stage, a phrase meaning to cry or shed tears.

clue.text: Arousing films, for example, using Beethoven's music, including his fourth

indicators.note: including means the symphony name takes in the extra letter

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony
the fourth letter of Beethoven is T

explanation.surface: Sexy films using a Beethoven score that includes his Fourth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his fourth' looks like the Fourth Symphony but means the fourth letter of Beethoven's name; 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic films are one form of sexually arousing material.

clue.text: See 5
Joined in editing page included in cut

indicators.note: included in places the page abbreviation inside the cutting word

parts.note: sliced means cut

explanation.surface: Film footage joined during editing, with a page included in the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Film editors joined lengths of film together, an editing term for joining.

clue.text: More austere in ultimate part, Mirren's 2006 role

parts.note: the stern is the rearmost part of a ship
Helen Mirren played the Queen in The Queen (2006), ER being Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Grimmer in the final role, Helen Mirren's Oscar-winning 2006 part.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of stern, meaning more severe or austere.

clue.text: C for Chaplin, say

definitions.meaning: the word for C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the first name of Chaplin the silent film comedian

explanation.definitionFit: The radio-alphabet code word for the letter C, and the comic actor's first name.

clue.text: Directors in vehicles, several holding Oscar, finally

indicators.note: holding means the word for several wraps around the final letter

parts.note: divers is an old word for several or sundry

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Oscar

explanation.surface: Film directors in cars, several clutching an Oscar at last.
explanation.definitionFit: The people who steer, or direct, cars and other vehicles.

clue.text: Not a winner this time around? Perhaps on a different occasion

definitions.text: Not a winner this time around? Perhaps on a different occasion

parts.words: Not a winner this time around? Perhaps on a different occasion
parts.note: a consolation to a losing nominee, also the title of Mike Leigh's 2010 film, nominated but not winning

explanation.surface: A consolation for an Oscar loser: maybe you will win some other time.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for some future occasion, and Mike Leigh's 2010 film that was nominated but did not win.

clue.text: McGraw in boxing movie

definitions.meaning: the first name of the Love Story actress surnamed MacGraw
Michael Mann's 2001 film about the heavyweight champion

explanation.definitionFit: First name of the actress MacGraw, and the 2001 biopic of the boxer once called Cassius Clay.

clue.text: Partial angle about odd dream for superhero

indicators.note: about places the slant word around the jumbled letters

parts.note: spin is a partial angle, a biased slant put on news

indicators.note: odd signals the letters of dream are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: A biased slant on a strange dream about a comic-book hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Parker's web-slinging alter ego is a Marvel comics superhero.

clue.text: Feeling of self-importance obvious in "The Godfather"

indicators.note: obvious in tells us the letters can be seen inside the film title

explanation.surface: Arrogance is evident in Coppola's mafia film.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflated sense of self, or conceit, is called this psychological term.

clue.text: Movie star large in reputation

indicators.note: in places the size letter inside the word for reputation

parts.note: note means fame or reputation, as in a person of note

explanation.surface: A big name in Hollywood with a large reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick, the American actor of 48 Hrs. and Cape Fear, is a film star.

clue.text: It was instrumental in making movie that got Holly Hunter an Oscar

definitions.text: It was instrumental in making movie that got Holly Hunter an Oscar

parts.words: It was instrumental in making movie that got Holly Hunter an Oscar
parts.note: instrumental read literally: a musical instrument gave its name to Jane Campion's 1993 film

explanation.surface: Something played a key role in the film that won Holly Hunter her Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Campion's 1993 film, for which Hunter won Best Actress, is named for this keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Lacking true grit, even retreating across river? Not so

indicators.note: across means the turned word stretches over the river letter
retreating means even is read going backwards

parts.note: less, as in 'less so', means not so much

explanation.surface: A coward without true grit, even retreating across a river; not so brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns EVEN into NEVE, and 'across' puts R inside it; True Grit also nods to the John Wayne Oscar film.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without nerve means lacking courage or pluck.
